name: Principles of Heredity & Selection

objectives.text: Match young animals to their parents based on observable traits such as color, markings, and size
Sort animal characteristics into traits passed down from parents and features caused by the animal's surroundings or care
Describe how offspring inherit traits from both their dam and their sire
Explain how producers choose animals with desirable traits as parents to improve the next generation of a herd or flock
Explain the difference between dominant and recessive traits using a livestock example such as black and red coat color or polled and horned cattle
Describe how genes carried on chromosomes are passed to offspring with each parent contributing one allele for each gene
Distinguish between genotype and phenotype and between homozygous and heterozygous animals for a single livestock trait
Construct a Punnett square to predict the probability of offspring traits from a single-trait livestock cross
Define inheritance terms used in animal breeding including dominant, recessive, codominant, incomplete dominance, homozygous, heterozygous, allele, and sex-linked
Explain codominant and incompletely dominant inheritance using livestock examples such as roan Shorthorn cattle or palomino horses
Calculate expected genotypic and phenotypic ratios for two-trait livestock crosses such as polled and coat color in cattle
Differentiate qualitative traits controlled by few genes from quantitative traits such as growth, milk yield, and carcass merit that are shaped by many genes and the environment

Identify inherited genetic defects that affect animal performance such as arthrogryposis multiplex in cattle, porcine stress syndrome in swine, and HYPP in horses and explain how carriers pass them on
Explain how heritability estimates determine how quickly a trait will respond to selection by comparing highly heritable traits with lowly heritable traits such as fertility
Calculate the expected response to selection per generation using heritability, selection differential, and generation interval
Calculate adjusted weights and within-group ratios from SAE herd or flock records to rank animals for selection
Interpret expected progeny differences and their accuracy values to compare the genetic merit of genetically superior sires with breed-average sires
Analyze an animal's pedigree and performance records to evaluate its genetic merit for a specific trait
Analyze how selecting for one trait can change genetically correlated traits such as birth weight and growth rate
Recommend breeding decisions using DNA test results such as genetic defect carrier status and genomic-enhanced EPDs
Justify the selection of specific mating pairs to achieve a desired genetic outcome while avoiding the production of affected offspring from carrier animals
Evaluate animals for theoretical purchase based on expected progeny differences, performance records, pedigrees, and a specified production scenario
Evaluate economic selection indexes such as maternal or terminal dollar values to rank breeding stock for the goals of a particular operation
Design a multi-generation selection plan that uses heritability estimates, expected progeny differences, and DNA data to improve a herd's genetics toward defined production goals

changes: Kept all six existing objectives as real competencies, lightly reworded (dam and sire language, broader dominant and recessive examples, Punnett square as construct). Added early-grade objectives on heritable versus environmental traits and the idea of selection, middle-grade objectives on genes, alleles, genotype, and phenotype, and high-school objectives on codominance and incomplete dominance, two-trait crosses, qualitative versus quantitative traits, genetic defects and carriers, heritability and response to selection, SAE record ratios, EPD and accuracy interpretation, correlated traits, DNA-based decisions, mating-pair justification, theoretical purchase evaluation, and economic selection indexes. The capstone plan now focuses on selection and leaves crossbreeding systems, AI, reproductive anatomy, and visual judging to sibling sub-topics. Standards were assigned only from grade 9 upward.
